12	# Bun Project Rules
13	
14	## Mandatory Context
15	
16	Before making any changes:
17	
18	1. Read the root `README.md` — its Documentation section lists every doc in reading order, as a Markdown table (or an equivalent linked list), each with a link and a description
19	2. Inspect all file names under `docs/` and subfolders in the current repository — some files may be missing from the README
20	3. Read files that appear relevant to the current task
21	4. Treat `docs/` as the source of truth for project-specific conventions and follow those documents over this file when they conflict
22	5. When an `rfc/` folder exists, treat its Accepted RFCs as binding versioned standards — follow them over `docs/` and this file when they conflict; see `rfc/README.md` for the convention
23	6. When a `principles/` folder exists, read its `README.md` and the principles relevant to the task — they are the long-lived values that standards and reviews appeal to; follow `rfc/` and `docs/` over them for concrete rules
24	
25	**Rule Markers Legend:**
26	
27	- 🤖 = Automated by linter (ESLint/Stylelint enforces this)
28	- 👤 = Human-enforced (requires manual review)
29	
30	## 1. Core Principles
31	
32	- 👤 Context first: Gather complete understanding before changes
33	- 👤 Pattern matching: Check existing codebase for similar implementations
34	- 👤 Progressive enhancement: Build incrementally, test frequently
35	- 👤 Functional/declarative patterns; avoid classes
36	- 👤 Keep dependencies minimal - prefer built-in features
37	- 👤 Every line of code must be used or removed
38	- 👤 The fewer lines of code the better
39	- 👤 Avoid code duplication - maximize reuse
40	- 👤 Do not over-engineer - only make directly requested changes. No abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite
41	- 👤 Surface assumptions and ambiguities before coding; if multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently
42	- 👤 Define verifiable success criteria before implementing (test, command, or observable behavior)
43	- 👤 Every changed line must trace to the request - no opportunistic refactors of adjacent code or unrelated formatting
44	- 👤 When deleting unused code, only remove orphans your changes created; mention pre-existing dead code instead of deleting it
45	- 👤 Be consistent with existing code style
46	- 👤 Do not remove existing code/comments unless necessary
47	- 👤 Write plan before changes, not report after — draft it via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` (if the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md)
48	
49	## 2. Architecture
50	
51	### 2.1 Technology Stack
52	
53	- Bun, TypeScript 6.x
54	- ESLint for linting
55	- Prettier for formatting
56	
57	### 2.2 Directory Layout
58	
59	- `scripts/` - Scripts
60	
61	## 3. Project Structure
62	
63	### 3.1 File Organization
64	
65	```
66	example.ts     # single module: a file, no directory
67	
68	example/       # multiple modules: a directory, no index.ts barrel
69	├── example.ts
70	├── example.test.ts
71	├── example.types.ts
72	└── example.module.css
73	```
74	
75	### 3.2 Import Rules
76	
77	- 🤖 Always import from actual files - never barrel files (`import/order`)
78	- 🤖 Import order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling
79	- 👤 No generic names (index.ts, init.ts) - use descriptive names
80	
81	## 4. Naming Conventions
82	
83	- 🤖 Variables/functions: camelCase (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)
84	- 🤖 Components/types/interfaces: PascalCase
85	- 🤖 No I prefix for interfaces
86	- 👤 Files: Components PascalCase, utilities camelCase
87	- 👤 Test files: `*.test.ts` suffix
88	- 🤖 Named exports only - no default exports (`import/no-default-export`)
89	- 👤 IMPORTANT: camelCase for constants (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE)
90	- 👤 Descriptive names with auxiliary verbs (isLoading, hasError)
91	
92	## 5. Development Setup
93	
94	- Bun 1.x (latest stable)
95	- `bun install` – Install dependencies
96	- `bun run` – Run script
97	- `bun run lint` / `bun run lint:fix` – Linting
98	- `bun run format` / `bun run format:check` – Formatting
99	- `bun run typecheck` – Type checking
100	- `bun test` – Run tests
101	
102	## 6. Common Standards
103	
104	### 6.1 JavaScript
105	
106	- 👤 Use async/await, not callbacks
107	- 🤖 Use template literals for string interpolation, not concatenation (`prefer-template`)
108	- 🤖 Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` (`prefer-object-has-own`)
109	- 👤 Use `for...of` for array iteration, avoid classical `for` loops
110	- 👤 Write pure functions - same input returns same output, no side effects
111	- 👤 Prefer immutable array methods (map, filter, spread) over mutating (push, splice)
112	- 🤖 Use destructuring to extract object/array values (`prefer-destructuring`)
113	- 🤖 Use strict equality `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=` (`eqeqeq`)
114	- 🤖 Never mutate function parameters (`no-param-reassign`)
115	- 🤖 Always throw Error objects, not primitives (`no-throw-literal`)
116	- 🤖 Always reject Promises with Error objects (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`)
117	- 🤖 Use rest params `...args` instead of `arguments` (`prefer-rest-params`)
118	- 🤖 Limit nesting depth to 2 levels max (`max-depth`)
119	- 🤖 Limit cyclomatic complexity - few conditional branches (`complexity`)
120	- 🤖 Use early returns (fail fast) instead of nested else (`no-else-return`)
121	- 🤖 Functions should be 100 lines max (`max-lines-per-function`)
122	
123	### 6.2 TypeScript
124	
125	- 🤖 Prefer interfaces over types (`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions`)
126	- 👤 Avoid enums; use const assertions
127	- 🤖 Never use @ts-ignore (`@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment`)
128	- 👤 No type assertions without runtime validation (use Zod)
129	- 👤 Return specific types, not generic (string → KnownCallOutcome)
130	- 👤 Use type guards for narrowing
131	- 👤 Use React.ComponentProps for extending props
132	- 👤 Ask user for type information when `any` is unavoidable
133	
134	### 6.3 Bun
135	
136	- 👤 Use ES6 imports, not CommonJS
137	- 🤖 Use fs/promises for file operations (`n/prefer-promises/fs`)
138	- 👤 Graceful shutdown with signal handlers
139	- 👤 Validate env variables at startup
140	- 🤖 Use `bun:` protocol prefix for built-in modules (`unicorn/prefer-node-protocol`)
141	- 👤 Extend Error class for custom errors with context properties
142	- 👤 Await promises before returning for complete stack traces
143	- 👤 Subscribe to 'error' events on EventEmitters and streams
144	
145	### 8.4 File Operations
146	
147	- 👤 Use `bun:fs/promises` for files < 100MB
148	- 👤 Use streams for files > 100MB
149	- 👤 Use `pipeline()` for stream chaining
150	- 👤 Use `import.meta.dirname` for module-relative paths
151	- 👤 Handle error codes: ENOENT, EACCES, etc.
152	- 👤 Always close file handles in finally blocks
153	
154	## 9. API Standards
155	
156	### 9.2 Zod
157	
158	- 👤 Schemas in scripts/schemas/ by domain
159	- 👤 Use .merge(), .partial(), .pick(), .omit()
160	- 👤 Use z.infer<> for types
161	- 👤 Add custom error messages
162	- 👤 Use .transform() for normalization
163	- 👤 Use .refine() for complex validation
164	
165	## 11. Documentation
166	
167	### 11.1 JSDoc
168	
169	- 👤 Every exported interface/type must have JSDoc
170	- 👤 File-level JSDoc for src/config/ modules
171	- 👤 Use @example where usage isn't obvious
172	- 👤 Use @see <link> to add links to documentation
173	- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
174	- 👤 No useless descriptions repeating function name
175	- 👤 Skip JSDoc only if no params AND obvious from name
176	- 👤 Use @deprecated <reason> to mark deprecated code
177	- 👤 All modules must have top level JSDoc with description and usage examples
178	
179	### 11.2 Code comments
180	
181	- 👤 Avoid obvious comments, only when necessary
182	- 👤 Avoid link to exact lines of code
183	- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
184	- 👤 Avoid duplicates comments — it means code must be refactored
185	- 👤 Use only `TODO` (planned improvement) or `FIXME` (known defect) for deferred work — no XXX/HACK/NOTE markers
186	- 👤 Format: `// TODO: <description>` / `// FIXME: <description>` — uppercase keyword, colon + single space
187	- 👤 Link every TODO/FIXME with `// @see <issue-url>` on the line immediately below — full issue URL, not a bare `#123` in the description
188	- 👤 Remove the TODO and its `@see` line when the linked issue closes
189	- 👤 Use `Skill(autopilot:todo-cleanup)` to create, link, and clean up TODO issues. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
190	
191	### 11.3 docs/ structure
192	
193	- 👤 Organize `docs/` as numbered chapters in reading order (`NN-topic.md`, plus `appendix-X-topic.md` for non-sequential references), matching the README Documentation order
194	
195	## 12. Performance
196	
197	- 👤 O(1) lookups: Use Object/Map, not Array.find()
198	- 👤 Avoid map/reduce/for combinations
199	- 👤 Pre-compute lookups, not in render
200	- 👤 Memoize data transformations creating objects/arrays
201	- 👤 Use React.memo with displayName for stable-prop components
202	- 👤 Use factory functions for handlers with parameters
203	- 👤 Profile with React DevTools before adding useMemo/useCallback
204	
205	## 13. Security
206	
207	- 👤 Validate all external input before processing
208	- 👤 Never trust user data in object operations
209	- 👤 Use crypto.timingSafeEqual() for secret comparison
210	- 👤 Never log or expose secrets, tokens, or PII (logs, error messages, API responses)
211	- 👤 Use exact versions in package.json (no ^ or ~)
212	- 👤 Never enable debug inspector in production
213	- 👤 Never pass untrusted data to Object.assign()
214	- 👤 Use Object.create(null) for user-provided keys
215	- 👤 Use bun ci in CI/CD, not bun install
216	- 👤 Run bun audit before deploying
217	- 🤖 Never use eval() or Function() constructor (`no-eval`)
218	- 👤 Avoid dynamic require()/import() with user-controlled paths
219	
220	## 14. Anti-Patterns
221	
222	- 🤖 No CommonJS require() - use ES6 imports
223	- 👤 No callback-based APIs - use Promise-based
224	- 🤖 No sync file operations in servers (`n/no-sync`)
225	- 👤 No direct process.exit() - use graceful shutdown
226	- 👤 No TailwindCSS/CSS-in-JS - use CSS Modules
227	- 👤 No barrel files (index.ts re-exports)
228	- 👤 No unused exports - delete immediately
229	- 👤 No commented-out code - delete it (recover from version control if needed)
230	- 👤 No empty catch blocks - never swallow errors; rethrow or handle with context
231	- 👤 No wrapper functions without added logic
232	- 👤 No Array.find() for lookups - use Map/Object
233	- 👤 No useEffect for state sync
234	- 👤 No inline functions in loops
235	- 👤 No incomplete configurations
236	- 👤 No raw `git commit` — use `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)`
237	- 👤 No raw `git checkout -b` / `git branch` — use `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)`
238	- 👤 No raw `gh pr create` — use `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)`
239	- 👤 No raw `gh issue create` — use `Skill(autopilot:issue-create)`
240	- 👤 No ad-hoc planning — use `Skill(autopilot:plan)`
241	
242	## 15. Git Workflow
243	
244	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository root is the binding standard for every branch, commit, PR, and issue operation — read the governing section before acting; never restate or improvise its rules
245	- 👤 Governing sections: "Branches" for branch names, "Commits" for commit messages, "PR Title" and "Special PR Prefixes" for PR titles, "PR Description" and "Magic Words" for PR bodies and issue linking, "How to Contribute" for issues
246	- 👤 The `Skill(autopilot:*)` commands in §16.1 implement these conventions — invoking the skill satisfies this section
247	- 👤 Never bypass validation hooks with `--no-verify` — fix the violation instead
248	
249	## 16. AI Assistant Workflow
250	
251	### 16.1 Claude Code
252	
253	- 👤 Use TodoWrite to track complex tasks
254	- 👤 Mark todos as completed immediately
255	- 👤 Parallel tool execution when possible
256	- 👤 Gather context before editing
257	- 👤 Use `gh` CLI for GitHub issues, PRs, comments, and Actions info
258	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Commit only via `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)` — no raw `git commit`, no `git commit -m`, no `--amend`, no exceptions. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
259	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create branches only via `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)` — no raw `git checkout -b`, `git branch`, or `git switch -c`. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
260	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create PRs only via `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)` — no raw `gh pr create` or web-UI PR creation. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
261	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create issues only via `Skill(autopilot:issue-create)` — no raw `gh issue create` or web-UI issue creation. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
262	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Plan only via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` — no ad-hoc implementation planning. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
263	
264	### 16.2 MCP Servers
265	
266	Prefer the project-registered MCP servers declared in the repo's own `.mcp.json`. The repository README and `docs/` are the authoritative list of which servers are registered and when to reach for each — consult them before hand-rolling work a registered server handles.
267	
268	- 👤 **Documentation servers** (context7, Ref, Exa) — look up docs for any technology, framework, or API (global/user servers, not project-registered)
269	- 👤 **Repomix MCP server** — pack the codebase into one digest and grep/read it for codebase-wide analysis instead of loading every file
270	
271	## 17. Code Review
272	
273	- All rules from AGENTS.md must be applied to the code review
274	
275	## 18. Graphify
276	
277	When `graphify-out/graph.json` exists, use the committed knowledge graph before broad source browsing:
278	
279	- For codebase questions, run `graphify query "<question>"` first. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts.
280	- Use `graphify-out/wiki/index.md` for broad navigation when it exists.
281	- Read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` only for broad architecture review or when targeted queries do not surface enough context.
282	- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).

- 🤖 = Automated by linter (ESLint/Stylelint enforces this)
- 👤 = Human-enforced (requires manual review)

## 1. Core Principles

- 👤 Context first: Gather complete understanding before changes
- 👤 Pattern matching: Check existing codebase for similar implementations
- 👤 Progressive enhancement: Build incrementally, test frequently
- 👤 Functional/declarative patterns; avoid classes
- 👤 Keep dependencies minimal - prefer built-in features
- 👤 Every line of code must be used or removed
- 👤 The fewer lines of code the better
- 👤 Avoid code duplication - maximize reuse
- 👤 Do not over-engineer - only make directly requested changes. No abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite
- 👤 Surface assumptions and ambiguities before coding; if multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently
- 👤 Define verifiable success criteria before implementing (test, command, or observable behavior)
- 👤 Every changed line must trace to the request - no opportunistic refactors of adjacent code or unrelated formatting
- 👤 When deleting unused code, only remove orphans your changes created; mention pre-existing dead code instead of deleting it
- 👤 Be consistent with existing code style
- 👤 Do not remove existing code/comments unless necessary
- 👤 Write plan before changes, not report after — draft it via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` (if the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md)

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Technology Stack

- Bun, TypeScript 6.x
- ESLint for linting
- Prettier for formatting

### 2.2 Directory Layout

- `scripts/` - Scripts

## 3. Project Structure

### 3.1 File Organization

```
example.ts     # single module: a file, no directory

example/       # multiple modules: a directory, no index.ts barrel
├── example.ts
├── example.test.ts
├── example.types.ts
└── example.module.css
```

### 3.2 Import Rules

- 🤖 Always import from actual files - never barrel files (`import/order`)
- 🤖 Import order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling
- 👤 No generic names (index.ts, init.ts) - use descriptive names

## 4. Naming Conventions

- 🤖 Variables/functions: camelCase (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)
- 🤖 Components/types/interfaces: PascalCase
- 🤖 No I prefix for interfaces
- 👤 Files: Components PascalCase, utilities camelCase
- 👤 Test files: `*.test.ts` suffix
- 🤖 Named exports only - no default exports (`import/no-default-export`)
- 👤 IMPORTANT: camelCase for constants (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE)
- 👤 Descriptive names with auxiliary verbs (isLoading, hasError)

## 5. Development Setup

- Bun 1.x (latest stable)
- `bun install` – Install dependencies
- `bun run` – Run script
- `bun run lint` / `bun run lint:fix` – Linting
- `bun run format` / `bun run format:check` – Formatting
- `bun run typecheck` – Type checking
- `bun test` – Run tests

## 6. Common Standards

### 6.1 JavaScript

- 👤 Use async/await, not callbacks
- 🤖 Use template literals for string interpolation, not concatenation (`prefer-template`)
- 🤖 Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` (`prefer-object-has-own`)
- 👤 Use `for...of` for array iteration, avoid classical `for` loops
- 👤 Write pure functions - same input returns same output, no side effects
- 👤 Prefer immutable array methods (map, filter, spread) over mutating (push, splice)
- 🤖 Use destructuring to extract object/array values (`prefer-destructuring`)
- 🤖 Use strict equality `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=` (`eqeqeq`)
- 🤖 Never mutate function parameters (`no-param-reassign`)
- 🤖 Always throw Error objects, not primitives (`no-throw-literal`)
- 🤖 Always reject Promises with Error objects (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`)
- 🤖 Use rest params `...args` instead of `arguments` (`prefer-rest-params`)
- 🤖 Limit nesting depth to 2 levels max (`max-depth`)
- 🤖 Limit cyclomatic complexity - few conditional branches (`complexity`)
- 🤖 Use early returns (fail fast) instead of nested else (`no-else-return`)
- 🤖 Functions should be 100 lines max (`max-lines-per-function`)

### 6.2 TypeScript

- 🤖 Prefer interfaces over types (`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions`)
- 👤 Avoid enums; use const assertions
- 🤖 Never use @ts-ignore (`@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment`)
- 👤 No type assertions without runtime validation (use Zod)
- 👤 Return specific types, not generic (string → KnownCallOutcome)
- 👤 Use type guards for narrowing
- 👤 Use React.ComponentProps for extending props
- 👤 Ask user for type information when `any` is unavoidable

### 6.3 Bun

- 👤 Use ES6 imports, not CommonJS
- 🤖 Use fs/promises for file operations (`n/prefer-promises/fs`)
- 👤 Graceful shutdown with signal handlers
- 👤 Validate env variables at startup
- 🤖 Use `bun:` protocol prefix for built-in modules (`unicorn/prefer-node-protocol`)
- 👤 Extend Error class for custom errors with context properties
- 👤 Await promises before returning for complete stack traces
- 👤 Subscribe to 'error' events on EventEmitters and streams

### 8.4 File Operations

- 👤 Use `bun:fs/promises` for files < 100MB
- 👤 Use streams for files > 100MB
- 👤 Use `pipeline()` for stream chaining
- 👤 Use `import.meta.dirname` for module-relative paths
- 👤 Handle error codes: ENOENT, EACCES, etc.
- 👤 Always close file handles in finally blocks

## 9. API Standards

### 9.2 Zod

- 👤 Schemas in scripts/schemas/ by domain
- 👤 Use .merge(), .partial(), .pick(), .omit()
- 👤 Use z.infer<> for types
- 👤 Add custom error messages
- 👤 Use .transform() for normalization
- 👤 Use .refine() for complex validation

## 11. Documentation

### 11.1 JSDoc

- 👤 Every exported interface/type must have JSDoc
- 👤 File-level JSDoc for src/config/ modules
- 👤 Use @example where usage isn't obvious
- 👤 Use @see <link> to add links to documentation
- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
- 👤 No useless descriptions repeating function name
- 👤 Skip JSDoc only if no params AND obvious from name
- 👤 Use @deprecated <reason> to mark deprecated code
- 👤 All modules must have top level JSDoc with description and usage examples

### 11.2 Code comments

- 👤 Avoid obvious comments, only when necessary
- 👤 Avoid link to exact lines of code
- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
- 👤 Avoid duplicates comments — it means code must be refactored
- 👤 Use only `TODO` (planned improvement) or `FIXME` (known defect) for deferred work — no XXX/HACK/NOTE markers
- 👤 Format: `// TODO: <description>` / `// FIXME: <description>` — uppercase keyword, colon + single space
- 👤 Link every TODO/FIXME with `// @see <issue-url>` on the line immediately below — full issue URL, not a bare `#123` in the description
- 👤 Remove the TODO and its `@see` line when the linked issue closes
- 👤 Use `Skill(autopilot:todo-cleanup)` to create, link, and clean up TODO issues. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md

### 11.3 docs/ structure

- 👤 Organize `docs/` as numbered chapters in reading order (`NN-topic.md`, plus `appendix-X-topic.md` for non-sequential references), matching the README Documentation order

## 12. Performance

- 👤 O(1) lookups: Use Object/Map, not Array.find()
- 👤 Avoid map/reduce/for combinations
- 👤 Pre-compute lookups, not in render
- 👤 Memoize data transformations creating objects/arrays
- 👤 Use React.memo with displayName for stable-prop components
- 👤 Use factory functions for handlers with parameters
- 👤 Profile with React DevTools before adding useMemo/useCallback

## 13. Security

- 👤 Validate all external input before processing
- 👤 Never trust user data in object operations
- 👤 Use crypto.timingSafeEqual() for secret comparison
- 👤 Never log or expose secrets, tokens, or PII (logs, error messages, API responses)
- 👤 Use exact versions in package.json (no ^ or ~)
- 👤 Never enable debug inspector in production
- 👤 Never pass untrusted data to Object.assign()
- 👤 Use Object.create(null) for user-provided keys
- 👤 Use bun ci in CI/CD, not bun install
- 👤 Run bun audit before deploying
- 🤖 Never use eval() or Function() constructor (`no-eval`)
- 👤 Avoid dynamic require()/import() with user-controlled paths

## 14. Anti-Patterns

- 🤖 No CommonJS require() - use ES6 imports
- 👤 No callback-based APIs - use Promise-based
- 🤖 No sync file operations in servers (`n/no-sync`)
- 👤 No direct process.exit() - use graceful shutdown
- 👤 No TailwindCSS/CSS-in-JS - use CSS Modules
- 👤 No barrel files (index.ts re-exports)
- 👤 No unused exports - delete immediately
- 👤 No commented-out code - delete it (recover from version control if needed)
- 👤 No empty catch blocks - never swallow errors; rethrow or handle with context
- 👤 No wrapper functions without added logic
- 👤 No Array.find() for lookups - use Map/Object
- 👤 No useEffect for state sync
- 👤 No inline functions in loops
- 👤 No incomplete configurations
- 👤 No raw `git commit` — use `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)`
- 👤 No raw `git checkout -b` / `git branch` — use `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)`
- 👤 No raw `gh pr create` — use `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)`
- 👤 No raw `gh issue create` — use `Skill(autopilot:issue-create)`
- 👤 No ad-hoc planning — use `Skill(autopilot:plan)`

## 15. Git Workflow

- 👤 **MANDATORY**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` in the repository root is the binding standard for every branch, commit, PR, and issue operation — read the governing section before acting; never restate or improvise its rules
- 👤 Governing sections: "Branches" for branch names, "Commits" for commit messages, "PR Title" and "Special PR Prefixes" for PR titles, "PR Description" and "Magic Words" for PR bodies and issue linking, "How to Contribute" for issues
- 👤 The `Skill(autopilot:*)` commands in §16.1 implement these conventions — invoking the skill satisfies this section
- 👤 Never bypass validation hooks with `--no-verify` — fix the violation instead

## 16. AI Assistant Workflow

### 16.1 Claude Code

- 👤 Use TodoWrite to track complex tasks
- 👤 Mark todos as completed immediately
- 👤 Parallel tool execution when possible
- 👤 Gather context before editing
- 👤 Use `gh` CLI for GitHub issues, PRs, comments, and Actions info
- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Commit only via `Skill(autopilot:commits-create)` — no raw `git commit`, no `git commit -m`, no `--amend`, no exceptions. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create branches only via `Skill(autopilot:branch-create)` — no raw `git checkout -b`, `git branch`, or `git switch -c`. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create PRs only via `Skill(autopilot:pr-create)` — no raw `gh pr create` or web-UI PR creation. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Create issues only via `Skill(autopilot:issue-create)` — no raw `gh issue create` or web-UI issue creation. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Plan only via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` — no ad-hoc implementation planning. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md

### 16.2 MCP Servers

Prefer the project-registered MCP servers declared in the repo's own `.mcp.json`. The repository README and `docs/` are the authoritative list of which servers are registered and when to reach for each — consult them before hand-rolling work a registered server handles.

- 👤 **Documentation servers** (context7, Ref, Exa) — look up docs for any technology, framework, or API (global/user servers, not project-registered)
- 👤 **Repomix MCP server** — pack the codebase into one digest and grep/read it for codebase-wide analysis instead of loading every file

## 17. Code Review

- All rules from AGENTS.md must be applied to the code review

## 18. Graphify

When `graphify-out/graph.json` exists, use the committed knowledge graph before broad source browsing:

- For codebase questions, run `graphify query "<question>"` first. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts.
- Use `graphify-out/wiki/index.md` for broad navigation when it exists.
- Read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` only for broad architecture review or when targeted queries do not surface enough context.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).

matches.line: Enable the `agents-md: true` input to also create an `AGENTS.md` symlink pointing to `CLAUDE.md`. This provides backward compatibility for teams transitioning between different AI assistant conventions while maintaining a single source of truth.

`AGENTS.md` is now the canonical rules file, with `CLAUDE.md` published as a Git symlink pointing to it — reversing the previous layout in a breaking change that requires a one-time workflow update before your next sync run.

The agent rules body now lands in `AGENTS.md`, which is the filename the broader agent ecosystem (Codex, Gemini CLI, and others) reads by convention. `CLAUDE.md` continues to be published alongside it, but now as a Git symlink (mode `120000`) that points at `AGENTS.md` rather than holding its own copy of the content. Both files are committed together in a single PR on every sync run — there is no configuration needed to enable this; it happens unconditionally.

This is now resolved: content entries whose destination is currently a symlink are detected and rewritten correctly, so both files always end up in the expected state after a sync run.

End-to-end data flow for [`agents-rules-sync`](../README.md), including how it composes with [`files-sync`](../../files-sync/README.md) to publish `AGENTS.md` and its `CLAUDE.md` symlink.

`files-sync` writes both `AGENTS.md` (regular file, carrying the rules body) and `CLAUDE.md` (Git symlink, mode `120000`) in the same commit and PR. `AGENTS.md` holds the content because it is the name the wider agent ecosystem reads; `CLAUDE.md` is the compatibility alias.

A repository synced by an earlier major has the pair the other way round — `CLAUDE.md` is the regular file, and `AGENTS.md` is either absent or a symlink pointing at it. Both cases converge in the first run after the upgrade, in one PR:
- **`AGENTS.md` absent** — the content entry creates it, and the symlink entry replaces the regular `CLAUDE.md` with a link.

- **`AGENTS.md` is a symlink** — the content branch detects the mode-`120000` destination and rewrites it as a regular file in the same commit that turns `CLAUDE.md` into the link. Without that mode check the two would end up pointing at each other; see [Why byte equality is not enough for a symlink destination](#why-byte-equality-is-not-enough-for-a-symlink-destination).

For symlink detection that is a deal-breaker. After the first run, the consumer's `CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md → <regular file>` chain would always look like the regular file's content via the Contents API, so we could never tell whether `CLAUDE.md` is already a symlink or a stale regular file.

The same server-side symlink resolution bites the **content** branch, in the one case where a content entry's destination is currently a link. That is precisely the state a repository is in while upgrading from the pre-inversion layout: `AGENTS.md` points at `CLAUDE.md`, which holds the rules body.

Read through the Contents API, that `AGENTS.md` resolves to the rules body — byte-identical to the source the entry is trying to write. Comparing bytes alone therefore concludes "no change" and leaves the link in place, while the symlink entry rewrites `CLAUDE.md` to point at `AGENTS.md`. The result is two links referencing each other with no regular file left in the cycle, and it is stable: every later run reaches the same "no change" verdict, so the sync can never repair itself.

1374:A repository synced by an earlier major has the pair the other way round — `CLAUDE.md` is the regular file, and `AGENTS.md` is either absent or a symlink pointing at it. Both cases converge in the first run after the upgrade, in one PR:
1376:- **`AGENTS.md` absent** — the content entry creates it, and the symlink entry replaces the regular `CLAUDE.md` with a link.

1377-- **`AGENTS.md` is a symlink** — the content branch detects the mode-`120000` destination and rewrites it as a regular file in the same commit that turns `CLAUDE.md` into the link. Without that mode check the two would end up pointing at each other; see [Why byte equality is not enough for a symlink destination](#why-byte-equality-is-not-enough-for-a-symlink-destination).

1383:For symlink detection that is a deal-breaker. After the first run, the consumer's `CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md → <regular file>` chain would always look like the regular file's content via the Contents API, so we could never tell whether `CLAUDE.md` is already a symlink or a stale regular file.

1389:The same server-side symlink resolution bites the **content** branch, in the one case where a content entry's destination is currently a link. That is precisely the state a repository is in while upgrading from the pre-inversion layout: `AGENTS.md` points at `CLAUDE.md`, which holds the rules body.

1391:Read through the Contents API, that `AGENTS.md` resolves to the rules body — byte-identical to the source the entry is trying to write. Comparing bytes alone therefore concludes "no change" and leaves the link in place, while the symlink entry rewrites `CLAUDE.md` to point at `AGENTS.md`. The result is two links referencing each other with no regular file left in the cycle, and it is stable: every later run reaches the same "no change" verdict, so the sync can never repair itself.

# Platform Standards — pr-review check details

Full rule bodies for the **Platform Standards** family of [pr-review §2.3](../SKILL.md#23-review-checks). Applies to every PR — no precondition.

**CHECK-PLAT-001: No issue IDs in commit messages** — Severity: blocker

GitHub issue references (`#123`, `Closes #123`) must NOT appear in commit messages. The PR description handles issue linking via magic words.

- Platform ref: `commitlint.config.ts` custom rule `no-issue-id`.

**CHECK-PLAT-002: Lint or type suppression comment (@ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error / eslint-disable)** — Severity: blocker

Zero tolerance for lint/type suppression comments. Any `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-nocheck`, `eslint-disable`, `eslint-disable-next-line` is a blocker.

**CHECK-PLAT-003: Wrong validation library** — Severity: suggestion

Data validation must use the stack-appropriate library, not manual validation or plain classes.

- **Bun / NodeJS+React / Bun+React+Tailwind / NodeJS+React+Tailwind**: must use Zod, not manual validation or plain interfaces for runtime validation.
- Skip if the diff does not add or modify validation logic.

content.text:
I read all four rule files and traced how they're consumed. I agree with the goal, but I'd push back on both halves of the mechanism — and I think you're aiming at the wrong 10% of the file.

## The 🤖 layer is genuinely broken

Not just redundant — factually wrong, and provably unmaintained:

- [`rules/Bun.md:77`](rules/Bun.md) marks "never barrel files" as enforced by `import/order`. That rule enforces *ordering*, not barrel bans. The very next line — the actual import-order rule — carries no citation. The citations are swapped.
- "No CommonJS require()" is 🤖 at line 222 with no rule name, and the same rule is 👤 at line 136. Same for barrel files: 🤖 at 77, 👤 at 227.
- §2.1 asserts "ESLint for linting" and §5 documents `bun run lint:fix`. **This repo has no ESLint config and no `lint:fix` script** — `lint` is `format:check && validate && turbo run typecheck`. The file's toolchain claim is false in its own home repo.

So the legend makes an unverifiable claim ("ESLint enforces this") from an upstream file that cannot see the consumer's toolchain. That's the same failure mode as inlining CONTRIBUTING.md constraint values — the thing this repo already fixed once.

## But "read the linter settings as mandatory context" would cost more than it saves

Three problems:

1. **Mandatory Context is paid every session.** It's `alwaysApply: true` in AGENTS.md. A 7th step that reads `eslint.config.js` usually returns `...tseslint.configs.recommended` plus a few overrides — near-zero information for a full file read. The effective rule set only comes from `eslint --print-config <file>`, which emits hundreds of rules. Neither form is a good trade for the 26 lines it replaces.
2. **The linter often doesn't exist.** Here it doesn't. Delete `eqeqeq`/`max-depth`/`no-param-reassign` and point at a config that isn't there, and the guidance is simply gone.
3. **Some 🤖 rules shape generation, not just verification.** `max-depth: 2`, `complexity`, `max-lines-per-function: 100`, interfaces-over-types, named-exports-only, no-barrels — the agent needs these *before* writing, or it produces a 4-deep 200-line function and then "fixes" it badly against a lint failure. A rule that changes what gets written earns its tokens even when a linter also checks it.

## What I'd do instead

**Split the 🤖 set by generation vs. verification**, rather than deleting it wholesale:

- **Delete (~14 rules, verification-only, mechanical to fix):** `eqeqeq`, `prefer-template`, `prefer-object-has-own`, `prefer-destructuring`, `no-throw-literal`, `prefer-promise-reject-errors`, `prefer-rest-params`, `no-else-return`, `ban-ts-comment`, `prefer-node-protocol`, `prefer-promises/fs`, `no-sync`, `no-eval`, the duplicate CommonJS line.
- **Keep (~12), but strip the marker and the rule-name citation** — the citation is the part that goes stale downstream. Keep the constraint in prose.
- **Replace the legend** with one line: your project's lint command is the authority on style; run it rather than hand-auditing. That's cheaper and more reliable than reading config, and it degrades gracefully when there's no linter.

## The size argument points somewhere else

Worth saying plainly: 🤖 is 26 of 282 lines in `Bun.md`. Removing every one of them saves under 10%. If the goal is a leaner AGENTS.md, the real weight is elsewhere — and it's more clearly wrong:

- **React rules sitting in the non-React Bun rule set** — `React.ComponentProps` (§6.2), `React.memo` / `useMemo` / React DevTools / "not in render" (§12), "No TailwindCSS/CSS-in-JS - use CSS Modules" (§14), "No useEffect for state sync" (§14).
- **Repo-specific paths leaked into a generic stack file** — §9.2 "Schemas in `scripts/schemas/` by domain" is this repo's layout, shipped to every consumer.
- **Broken numbering** — §6 → "8.4" → §9 (only 9.2) → §11, no §7/§8/§10. Sections were deleted without renumbering, which is itself evidence nobody has audited this file end to end.

That cleanup is bigger, safer, and doesn't require any claim about the consumer's toolchain.

## Blast radius

All four rule files are near-identical (~206 differing lines out of ~400, mostly React/Tailwind sections), so any edit lands in all four. **No test pins their content** — the only `rules/*.md` references in tests are fixture path strings in `agents-rules-sync`, `agents-skills-sync`, and `files-sync`. They *are* prettier-enforced, and they're in `turbo.json`'s `test.inputs`, so an edit invalidates every member's test cache.

Want me to scope this as one change or two? My preference is two: the inapplicable-content + numbering cleanup first (uncontroversial, bigger win), then the 🤖 split as a follow-up, since that one changes a documented convention and deserves its own review.

11	
12	# NodeJS + React Project Rules
13	
14	## Mandatory Context
15	
16	Before making any changes:
17	
18	1. Read the root `README.md` — its Documentation section lists every doc in reading order, as a Markdown table (or an equivalent linked list), each with a link and a description
19	2. Inspect all file names under `docs/` and subfolders in the current repository — some files may be missing from the README
20	3. Read files that appear relevant to the current task
21	4. Treat `docs/` as the source of truth for project-specific conventions and follow those documents over this file when they conflict
22	5. When an `rfc/` folder exists, treat its Accepted RFCs as binding versioned standards — follow them over `docs/` and this file when they conflict; see `rfc/README.md` for the convention
23	6. When a `principles/` folder exists, read its `README.md` and the principles relevant to the task — they are the long-lived values that standards and reviews appeal to; follow `rfc/` and `docs/` over them for concrete rules
24	
25	**Rule Markers Legend:**
26	
27	- 🤖 = Automated by linter (ESLint/Stylelint enforces this)
28	- 👤 = Human-enforced (requires manual review)
29	
30	## 1. Core Principles
31	
32	- 👤 Context first: Gather complete understanding before changes
33	- 👤 Pattern matching: Check existing codebase for similar implementations
34	- 👤 Progressive enhancement: Build incrementally, test frequently
35	- 👤 Functional/declarative patterns; avoid classes
36	- 👤 Keep dependencies minimal - prefer built-in features
37	- 👤 Every line of code must be used or removed
38	- 👤 The fewer lines of code the better
39	- 👤 Avoid code duplication - maximize reuse
40	- 👤 Do not over-engineer - only make directly requested changes. No abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite
41	- 👤 Surface assumptions and ambiguities before coding; if multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently
42	- 👤 Define verifiable success criteria before implementing (test, command, or observable behavior)
43	- 👤 Every changed line must trace to the request - no opportunistic refactors of adjacent code or unrelated formatting
44	- 👤 When deleting unused code, only remove orphans your changes created; mention pre-existing dead code instead of deleting it
45	- 👤 Be consistent with existing code style
46	- 👤 Write failing tests first, then write code to pass tests
47	- 👤 Run tests after any code changes
48	- 👤 Do not remove existing code/comments unless necessary
49	- 👤 Write plan before changes, not report after — draft it via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` (if the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md)
50	
51	## 2. Architecture
52	
53	### 2.1 Technology Stack
54	
55	- Full-stack React + Node.js with Express
56	- TypeScript 6.x, React 19, Vite
57	- npm or pnpm for package management
58	- Prisma (migrations) + Kysely (application ORM)
59	- PostgreSQL database
60	- oRPC or tRPC for API, Zod for validation
61	- Mantine for UI components
62	- React Router for routing
63	- React Query for data fetching
64	- Vitest for testing
65	- BetterAuth for authentication
66	- ESLint for linting
67	- Prettier for formatting
68	- CSS Modules for styling
69	
70	## 3. Project Structure
71	
72	### 3.1 File Organization
73	
74	```
75	example.ts     # single module: a file, no directory
76	
77	example/       # multiple modules: a directory, no index.ts barrel
78	├── example.ts
79	├── example.test.ts
80	├── example.types.ts
81	└── example.module.css
82	```
83	
84	- 👤 Order code top-down by importance: public entry points and core domain logic first, lower-level helpers and utilities last
85	
86	### 3.2 Import Rules
87	
88	- 🤖 Always import from actual files - never barrel files (`import/order`)
89	- 🤖 Import order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling
90	- 🤖 Client cannot import server code (`import/no-restricted-paths`)
91	- 👤 No generic names (index.ts, init.ts) - use descriptive names
92	
93	### 3.3 CSS Modules
94	
95	- 👤 Use `.module.css` files, not plain CSS
96	- 👤 Import as `import styles from "./X.module.css"`
97	- 👤 Use `className={styles.ClassName}`
98	
99	## 4. Naming Conventions
100	
101	- 🤖 Variables/functions: camelCase (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)
102	- 🤖 Components/types/interfaces: PascalCase
103	- 🤖 No I prefix for interfaces
104	- 👤 Hooks: camelCase with 'use' prefix
105	- 👤 Files: Components PascalCase, utilities camelCase
106	- 👤 Test files: `*.test.ts` suffix
107	- 🤖 Named exports only - no default exports (`import/no-default-export`)
108	- 👤 IMPORTANT: camelCase for constants (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE)
109	- 👤 Descriptive names with auxiliary verbs (isLoading, hasError)
110	
111	## 5. Development Setup
112	
113	- Node.js 24 LTS via nvm
114	- 👤 Inspect @package.json before assuming scripts or package-manager commands
115	
116	## 6. Environment Variables
117	
118	- 🤖 No direct process.env or import.meta.env outside config (`no-restricted-syntax`)
119	- 👤 Client: `import.meta.env.VITE_*`
120	- 👤 Server: `process.env.*`
121	- 👤 All variables have fallback defaults
122	- 👤 Use .env.example as template
123	
124	## 7. Client-Side Standards
125	
126	### 7.1 React
127	
128	- 🤖 Arrow function components only (`react/function-component-definition`)
129	- 👤 Use `nullable()` helper for conditional rendering (not &&)
130	- 🤖 Props: interfaces, not types
131	- 👤 Composition over inheritance
132	- 👤 useCallback for handlers passed as props
133	- 👤 useMemo for expensive computations
134	- 🤖 No inline arrow functions in JSX (`react/jsx-no-bind`)
135	- 👤 Components > 200 lines should be split
136	- 👤 Use Suspense for data fetching
137	- 👤 Use useSuspenseQuery instead of useQuery
138	- 🤖 One component per file (`react/no-multi-comp`)
139	- 🤖 Never use array index as `key` prop (`react/no-array-index-key`)
140	- 🤖 Self-close components with no children (`react/self-closing-comp`)
141	- 🤖 Avoid `style` prop, use CSS Modules instead (`react/forbid-component-props`)
142	- 👤 Proactively identify reusable component patterns
143	
144	### 7.2 JavaScript
145	
146	- 👤 Use async/await, not callbacks
147	- 🤖 Use template literals for string interpolation, not concatenation (`prefer-template`)
148	- 🤖 Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` (`prefer-object-has-own`)
149	- 👤 Use `for...of` for array iteration, avoid classical `for` loops
150	- 👤 Write pure functions - same input returns same output, no side effects
151	- 👤 Prefer immutable array methods (map, filter, spread) over mutating (push, splice)
152	- 🤖 Use destructuring to extract object/array values (`prefer-destructuring`)
153	- 🤖 Use strict equality `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=` (`eqeqeq`)
154	- 🤖 Never mutate function parameters (`no-param-reassign`)
155	- 🤖 Always throw Error objects, not primitives (`no-throw-literal`)
156	- 🤖 Always reject Promises with Error objects (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`)
157	- 🤖 Use rest params `...args` instead of `arguments` (`prefer-rest-params`)
158	- 🤖 Limit nesting depth to 2 levels max (`max-depth`)
159	- 🤖 Limit cyclomatic complexity - few conditional branches (`complexity`)
160	- 🤖 Use early returns (fail fast) instead of nested else (`no-else-return`)
161	- 🤖 Functions should be 100 lines max (`max-lines-per-function`)
162	
163	### 7.3 TypeScript
164	
165	- 🤖 Prefer interfaces over types (`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions`)
166	- 👤 Avoid enums; use const assertions
167	- 🤖 Never use @ts-ignore (`@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment`)
168	- 👤 No type assertions without runtime validation (use Zod)
169	- 👤 Return specific types, not generic (string → KnownCallOutcome)
170	- 👤 Use type guards for narrowing
171	- 👤 Use React.ComponentProps for extending props
172	- 👤 Ask user for type information when `any` is unavoidable
173	
174	### 7.4 State Management
175	
176	- 👤 Don't useEffect to sync state - causes loops
177	- 👤 Prefer derived state (useMemo) over synced state
178	- 👤 Map/Set for lookups, Array only when order matters
179	- 👤 Initialize text states with "", not undefined
180	- 👤 Keep state in the lowest component that needs it
181	- 👤 Split state into individual pieces, not entire objects
182	
183	### 7.5 React Query
184	
185	- 👤 Handle isLoading, error, data states (use Suspense)
186	- 👤 Set appropriate staleTime
187	- 👤 Invalidate queries after mutations
188	- 👤 Use onError for specific handling
189	- 👤 DevTools in development only
190	
191	### 7.6 Mantine
192	
193	- 👤 Use Mantine components from @mantine/core
194	- 👤 Use @mantine/hooks for common hooks
195	- 👤 Use @mantine/form with zodResolver
196	- 👤 Wrap Mantine components in project-level components for reusability
197	
198	## 8. Server-Side Standards
199	
200	### 8.1 NodeJS
201	
202	- 👤 Use ES6 imports, not CommonJS
203	- 🤖 Use fs/promises for file operations (`n/prefer-promises/fs`)
204	- 👤 Graceful shutdown with signal handlers
205	- 👤 Validate env variables at startup
206	- 🤖 Use `node:` protocol prefix for built-in modules (`unicorn/prefer-node-protocol`)
207	- 👤 Extend Error class for custom errors with context properties
208	- 👤 Await promises before returning for complete stack traces
209	- 👤 Subscribe to 'error' events on EventEmitters and streams
210	
211	### 8.2 Express
212	
213	- 👤 Use helmet for security headers
214	- 👤 Use compression middleware
215	- 👤 Middleware pattern for request handling
216	
217	### 8.3 Database (Prisma/Kysely)
218	
219	- 👤 Prisma: migrations and type generation ONLY
220	- 👤 Kysely: ALL application queries
221	- 👤 Never use Prisma Client in application code
222	- 👤 Use explicit junction tables
223	- 👤 Use `/// @kyselyType()` in schema.prisma for typed Json fields (never edit kysely.ts directly)
224	
225	### 8.4 File Operations
226	
227	- 👤 Use `node:fs/promises` for files < 100MB
228	- 👤 Use streams for files > 100MB
229	- 👤 Use `pipeline()` for stream chaining
230	- 👤 Use `import.meta.dirname` for module-relative paths
231	- 👤 Handle error codes: ENOENT, EACCES, etc.
232	- 👤 Always close file handles in finally blocks
233	
234	## 9. API Standards
235

273	- 👤 ES module imports require .js extensions
274	- 👤 Uses Playwright under the hood, use Playwright MCP for UI tests

276	- 👤 Never assume element types/labels without verification

279	## 11. Documentation
280	
281	### 11.1 JSDoc
282	
283	- 👤 Every exported interface/type must have JSDoc
284	- 👤 File-level JSDoc for config modules
285	- 👤 Use @example where usage isn't obvious
286	- 👤 Use @see <link> to add links to documentation
287	- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
288	- 👤 No useless descriptions repeating function name
289	- 👤 Skip JSDoc only if no params AND obvious from name
290	- 👤 Use @deprecated <reason> to mark deprecated code
291	- 👤 All modules must have top level JSDoc with description and usage examples
292	
293	### 11.2 Code comments
294	
295	- 👤 Avoid obvious comments, only when necessary
296	- 👤 Avoid link to exact lines of code
297	- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
298	- 👤 Avoid duplicates comments — it means code must be refactored
299	- 👤 Use only `TODO` (planned improvement) or `FIXME` (known defect) for deferred work — no XXX/HACK/NOTE markers
300	- 👤 Format: `// TODO: <description>` / `// FIXME: <description>` — uppercase keyword, colon + single space
301	- 👤 Link every TODO/FIXME with `// @see <issue-url>` on the line immediately below — full issue URL, not a bare `#123` in the description
302	- 👤 Remove the TODO and its `@see` line when the linked issue closes
303	- 👤 Use `Skill(autopilot:todo-cleanup)` to create, link, and clean up TODO issues. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md
304	
305	### 11.3 docs/ structure
306	
307	- 👤 Organize `docs/` as numbered chapters in reading order (`NN-topic.md`, plus `appendix-X-topic.md` for non-sequential references), matching the README Documentation order

310

312	- 👤 Avoid map/reduce/for combinations
313	- 👤 Pre-compute lookups, not in render
314	- 👤 Memoize data transformations creating objects/arrays

316	- 👤 Use factory functions for handlers with parameters

320

322	- 👤 Never trust user data in object operations

378	- 👤 **MANDATORY**: Plan only via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` — no ad-hoc implementation planning. If the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md

# NodeJS + React Project Rules

## Mandatory Context

Before making any changes:

1. Read the root `README.md` — its Documentation section lists every doc in reading order, as a Markdown table (or an equivalent linked list), each with a link and a description
2. Inspect all file names under `docs/` and subfolders in the current repository — some files may be missing from the README
3. Read files that appear relevant to the current task
4. Treat `docs/` as the source of truth for project-specific conventions and follow those documents over this file when they conflict
5. When an `rfc/` folder exists, treat its Accepted RFCs as binding versioned standards — follow them over `docs/` and this file when they conflict; see `rfc/README.md` for the convention
6. When a `principles/` folder exists, read its `README.md` and the principles relevant to the task — they are the long-lived values that standards and reviews appeal to; follow `rfc/` and `docs/` over them for concrete rules

**Rule Markers Legend:**

- 🤖 = Automated by linter (ESLint/Stylelint enforces this)
- 👤 = Human-enforced (requires manual review)

## 1. Core Principles

- 👤 Context first: Gather complete understanding before changes
- 👤 Pattern matching: Check existing codebase for similar implementations
- 👤 Progressive enhancement: Build incrementally, test frequently
- 👤 Functional/declarative patterns; avoid classes
- 👤 Keep dependencies minimal - prefer built-in features
- 👤 Every line of code must be used or removed
- 👤 The fewer lines of code the better
- 👤 Avoid code duplication - maximize reuse
- 👤 Do not over-engineer - only make directly requested changes. No abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite
- 👤 Surface assumptions and ambiguities before coding; if multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently
- 👤 Define verifiable success criteria before implementing (test, command, or observable behavior)
- 👤 Every changed line must trace to the request - no opportunistic refactors of adjacent code or unrelated formatting
- 👤 When deleting unused code, only remove orphans your changes created; mention pre-existing dead code instead of deleting it
- 👤 Be consistent with existing code style
- 👤 Write failing tests first, then write code to pass tests
- 👤 Run tests after any code changes
- 👤 Do not remove existing code/comments unless necessary
- 👤 Write plan before changes, not report after — draft it via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` (if the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md)

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Technology Stack

- Full-stack React + Node.js with Express
- TypeScript 6.x, React 19, Vite
- npm or pnpm for package management
- Prisma (migrations) + Kysely (application ORM)
- PostgreSQL database
- oRPC or tRPC for API, Zod for validation
- Mantine for UI components
- React Router for routing
- React Query for data fetching
- Vitest for testing
- BetterAuth for authentication
- ESLint for linting
- Prettier for formatting
- CSS Modules for styling

## 3. Project Structure

### 3.1 File Organization

```
example.ts     # single module: a file, no directory

example/       # multiple modules: a directory, no index.ts barrel
├── example.ts
├── example.test.ts
├── example.types.ts
└── example.module.css
```

- 👤 Order code top-down by importance: public entry points and core domain logic first, lower-level helpers and utilities last

### 3.2 Import Rules

- 🤖 Always import from actual files - never barrel files (`import/order`)
- 🤖 Import order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling
- 🤖 Client cannot import server code (`import/no-restricted-paths`)
- 👤 No generic names (index.ts, init.ts) - use descriptive names

### 3.3 CSS Modules

- 👤 Use `.module.css` files, not plain CSS
- 👤 Import as `import styles from "./X.module.css"`
- 👤 Use `className={styles.ClassName}`

## 4. Naming Conventions

- 🤖 Variables/functions: camelCase (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)
- 🤖 Components/types/interfaces: PascalCase
- 🤖 No I prefix for interfaces
- 👤 Hooks: camelCase with 'use' prefix
- 👤 Files: Components PascalCase, utilities camelCase
- 👤 Test files: `*.test.ts` suffix
- 🤖 Named exports only - no default exports (`import/no-default-export`)
- 👤 IMPORTANT: camelCase for constants (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE)
- 👤 Descriptive names with auxiliary verbs (isLoading, hasError)

## 5. Development Setup

- Node.js 24 LTS via nvm
- 👤 Inspect @package.json before assuming scripts or package-manager commands

## 6. Environment Variables

- 🤖 No direct process.env or import.meta.env outside config (`no-restricted-syntax`)
- 👤 Client: `import.meta.env.VITE_*`
- 👤 Server: `process.env.*`
- 👤 All variables have fallback defaults
- 👤 Use .env.example as template

## 7. Client-Side Standards

### 7.1 React

- 🤖 Arrow function components only (`react/function-component-definition`)
- 👤 Use `nullable()` helper for conditional rendering (not &&)
- 🤖 Props: interfaces, not types
- 👤 Composition over inheritance
- 👤 useCallback for handlers passed as props
- 👤 useMemo for expensive computations
- 🤖 No inline arrow functions in JSX (`react/jsx-no-bind`)
- 👤 Components > 200 lines should be split
- 👤 Use Suspense for data fetching
- 👤 Use useSuspenseQuery instead of useQuery
- 🤖 One component per file (`react/no-multi-comp`)
- 🤖 Never use array index as `key` prop (`react/no-array-index-key`)
- 🤖 Self-close components with no children (`react/self-closing-comp`)
- 🤖 Avoid `style` prop, use CSS Modules instead (`react/forbid-component-props`)
- 👤 Proactively identify reusable component patterns

### 7.2 JavaScript

- 👤 Use async/await, not callbacks
- 🤖 Use template literals for string interpolation, not concatenation (`prefer-template`)
- 🤖 Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` (`prefer-object-has-own`)
- 👤 Use `for...of` for array iteration, avoid classical `for` loops
- 👤 Write pure functions - same input returns same output, no side effects
- 👤 Prefer immutable array methods (map, filter, spread) over mutating (push, splice)
- 🤖 Use destructuring to extract object/array values (`prefer-destructuring`)
- 🤖 Use strict equality `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=` (`eqeqeq`)
- 🤖 Never mutate function parameters (`no-param-reassign`)
- 🤖 Always throw Error objects, not primitives (`no-throw-literal`)
- 🤖 Always reject Promises with Error objects (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`)
- 🤖 Use rest params `...args` instead of `arguments` (`prefer-rest-params`)
- 🤖 Limit nesting depth to 2 levels max (`max-depth`)
- 🤖 Limit cyclomatic complexity - few conditional branches (`complexity`)
- 🤖 Use early returns (fail fast) instead of nested else (`no-else-return`)
- 🤖 Functions should be 100 lines max (`max-lines-per-function`)

### 7.3 TypeScript

- 🤖 Prefer interfaces over types (`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions`)
- 👤 Avoid enums; use const assertions
- 🤖 Never use @ts-ignore (`@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment`)
- 👤 No type assertions without runtime validation (use Zod)
- 👤 Return specific types, not generic (string → KnownCallOutcome)
- 👤 Use type guards for narrowing
- 👤 Use React.ComponentProps for extending props
- 👤 Ask user for type information when `any` is unavoidable

### 7.4 State Management

- 👤 Don't useEffect to sync state - causes loops
- 👤 Prefer derived state (useMemo) over synced state
- 👤 Map/Set for lookups, Array only when order matters
- 👤 Initialize text states with "", not undefined
- 👤 Keep state in the lowest component that needs it
- 👤 Split state into individual pieces, not entire objects

### 7.5 React Query

- 👤 Handle isLoading, error, data states (use Suspense)
- 👤 Set appropriate staleTime
- 👤 Invalidate queries after mutations
- 👤 Use onError for specific handling
- 👤 DevTools in development only

### 7.6 Mantine

- 👤 Use Mantine components from @mantine/core
- 👤 Use @mantine/hooks for common hooks
- 👤 Use @mantine/form with zodResolver
- 👤 Wrap Mantine components in project-level components for reusability

## 8. Server-Side Standards

### 8.1 NodeJS

- 👤 Use ES6 imports, not CommonJS
- 🤖 Use fs/promises for file operations (`n/prefer-promises/fs`)
- 👤 Graceful shutdown with signal handlers
- 👤 Validate env variables at startup
- 🤖 Use `node:` protocol prefix for built-in modules (`unicorn/prefer-node-protocol`)
- 👤 Extend Error class for custom errors with context properties
- 👤 Await promises before returning for complete stack traces
- 👤 Subscribe to 'error' events on EventEmitters and streams

### 8.2 Express

- 👤 Use helmet for security headers
- 👤 Use compression middleware
- 👤 Middleware pattern for request handling

### 8.3 Database (Prisma/Kysely)

- 👤 Prisma: migrations and type generation ONLY
- 👤 Kysely: ALL application queries
- 👤 Never use Prisma Client in application code
- 👤 Use explicit junction tables
- 👤 Use `/// @kyselyType()` in schema.prisma for typed Json fields (never edit kysely.ts directly)

### 8.4 File Operations

- 👤 Use `node:fs/promises` for files < 100MB
- 👤 Use streams for files > 100MB
- 👤 Use `pipeline()` for stream chaining
- 👤 Use `import.meta.dirname` for module-relative paths
- 👤 Handle error codes: ENOENT, EACCES, etc.
- 👤 Always close file handles in finally blocks

## 9. API Standards

- 👤 **Playwright MCP server** — persistent, exploratory UI verification with `browser_snapshot`; prefer the token-efficient `@playwright/cli` CLI for high-throughput agent runs
- 👤 **Chrome DevTools MCP server** — performance traces, network inspection, console debugging
- 👤 **Repomix MCP server** — pack the codebase into one digest and grep/read it for codebase-wide analysis instead of loading every file

## 17. Code Review

- All rules from AGENTS.md must be applied to the code review

## 18. Graphify

When `graphify-out/graph.json` exists, use the committed knowledge graph before broad source browsing:

- For codebase questions, run `graphify query "<question>"` first. Use `graphify path "<A>" "<B>"` for relationships and `graphify explain "<concept>"` for focused concepts.
- Use `graphify-out/wiki/index.md` for broad navigation when it exists.
- Read `graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md` only for broad architecture review or when targeted queries do not surface enough context.
- After modifying code, run `graphify update .` to keep the graph current (AST-only, no API cost).

14	## Mandatory Context
15	
16	Before making any changes:
17	
18	1. Read the root `README.md` — its Documentation section lists every doc in reading order, as a Markdown table (or an equivalent linked list), each with a link and a description

23	6. When a `principles/` folder exists, read its `README.md` and the principles relevant to the task — they are the long-lived values that standards and reviews appeal to; follow `rfc/` and `docs/` over them for concrete rules
24

26

30	## 1. Core Principles
31	
32	- 👤 Context first: Gather complete understanding before changes
33	- 👤 Pattern matching: Check existing codebase for similar implementations
34	- 👤 Progressive enhancement: Build incrementally, test frequently
35	- 👤 Functional/declarative patterns; avoid classes
36	- 👤 Keep dependencies minimal - prefer built-in features
37	- 👤 Every line of code must be used or removed
38	- 👤 The fewer lines of code the better
39	- 👤 Avoid code duplication - maximize reuse
40	- 👤 Do not over-engineer - only make directly requested changes. No abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios. If 200 lines could be 50, rewrite
41	- 👤 Surface assumptions and ambiguities before coding; if multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently
42	- 👤 Define verifiable success criteria before implementing (test, command, or observable behavior)
43	- 👤 Every changed line must trace to the request - no opportunistic refactors of adjacent code or unrelated formatting
44	- 👤 When deleting unused code, only remove orphans your changes created; mention pre-existing dead code instead of deleting it
45	- 👤 Be consistent with existing code style
46	- 👤 Do not remove existing code/comments unless necessary
47	- 👤 Write plan before changes, not report after — draft it via `Skill(autopilot:plan)` (if the autopilot plugin is not installed, follow CONTRIBUTING.md)
48	
49	## 2. Architecture
50	
51	### 2.1 Technology Stack
52	
53	- Bun, TypeScript 6.x
54	- ESLint for linting
55	- Prettier for formatting
56	
57	### 2.2 Directory Layout
58	
59	- `scripts/` - Scripts
60	
61	## 3. Project Structure
62	
63	### 3.1 File Organization
64	
65	```
66	example.ts     # single module: a file, no directory
67	
68	example/       # multiple modules: a directory, no index.ts barrel
69	├── example.ts
70	├── example.test.ts
71	├── example.types.ts
72	└── example.module.css
73	```
74	
75	### 3.2 Import Rules
76	
77	- 🤖 Always import from actual files - never barrel files (`import/order`)
78	- 🤖 Import order: builtin → external → internal → parent → sibling
79	- 👤 No generic names (index.ts, init.ts) - use descriptive names
80	
81	## 4. Naming Conventions
82	
83	- 🤖 Variables/functions: camelCase (`@typescript-eslint/naming-convention`)
84	- 🤖 Components/types/interfaces: PascalCase
85	- 🤖 No I prefix for interfaces
86	- 👤 Files: Components PascalCase, utilities camelCase
87	- 👤 Test files: `*.test.ts` suffix
88	- 🤖 Named exports only - no default exports (`import/no-default-export`)
89	- 👤 IMPORTANT: camelCase for constants (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE)
90	- 👤 Descriptive names with auxiliary verbs (isLoading, hasError)
91	
92	## 5. Development Setup
93	
94	- Bun 1.x (latest stable)
95	- `bun install` – Install dependencies
96	- `bun run` – Run script
97	- `bun run lint` / `bun run lint:fix` – Linting
98	- `bun run format` / `bun run format:check` – Formatting
99	- `bun run typecheck` – Type checking
100	- `bun test` – Run tests
101	
102	## 6. Common Standards
103	
104	### 6.1 JavaScript
105	
106	- 👤 Use async/await, not callbacks
107	- 🤖 Use template literals for string interpolation, not concatenation (`prefer-template`)
108	- 🤖 Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` (`prefer-object-has-own`)
109	- 👤 Use `for...of` for array iteration, avoid classical `for` loops
110	- 👤 Write pure functions - same input returns same output, no side effects
111	- 👤 Prefer immutable array methods (map, filter, spread) over mutating (push, splice)
112	- 🤖 Use destructuring to extract object/array values (`prefer-destructuring`)
113	- 🤖 Use strict equality `===` and `!==`, never `==` or `!=` (`eqeqeq`)
114	- 🤖 Never mutate function parameters (`no-param-reassign`)
115	- 🤖 Always throw Error objects, not primitives (`no-throw-literal`)
116	- 🤖 Always reject Promises with Error objects (`prefer-promise-reject-errors`)
117	- 🤖 Use rest params `...args` instead of `arguments` (`prefer-rest-params`)
118	- 🤖 Limit nesting depth to 2 levels max (`max-depth`)
119	- 🤖 Limit cyclomatic complexity - few conditional branches (`complexity`)
120	- 🤖 Use early returns (fail fast) instead of nested else (`no-else-return`)
121	- 🤖 Functions should be 100 lines max (`max-lines-per-function`)
122	
123	### 6.2 TypeScript
124	
125	- 🤖 Prefer interfaces over types (`@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-definitions`)
126	- 👤 Avoid enums; use const assertions
127	- 🤖 Never use @ts-ignore (`@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment`)
128	- 👤 No type assertions without runtime validation (use Zod)
129	- 👤 Return specific types, not generic (string → KnownCallOutcome)
130	- 👤 Use type guards for narrowing
131	- 👤 Use React.ComponentProps for extending props
132	- 👤 Ask user for type information when `any` is unavoidable
133	
134	### 6.3 Bun
135	
136	- 👤 Use ES6 imports, not CommonJS
137	- 🤖 Use fs/promises for file operations (`n/prefer-promises/fs`)
138	- 👤 Graceful shutdown with signal handlers
139	- 👤 Validate env variables at startup
140	- 🤖 Use `bun:` protocol prefix for built-in modules (`unicorn/prefer-node-protocol`)
141	- 👤 Extend Error class for custom errors with context properties
142	- 👤 Await promises before returning for complete stack traces
143	- 👤 Subscribe to 'error' events on EventEmitters and streams
144	
145	### 8.4 File Operations
146	
147	- 👤 Use `bun:fs/promises` for files < 100MB
148	- 👤 Use streams for files > 100MB
149	- 👤 Use `pipeline()` for stream chaining
150	- 👤 Use `import.meta.dirname` for module-relative paths
151	- 👤 Handle error codes: ENOENT, EACCES, etc.
152	- 👤 Always close file handles in finally blocks
153	
154	## 9. API Standards
155	
156	### 9.2 Zod
157	
158	- 👤 Schemas in scripts/schemas/ by domain
159	- 👤 Use .merge(), .partial(), .pick(), .omit()
160	- 👤 Use z.infer<> for types

162	- 👤 Use .transform() for normalization
163	- 👤 Use .refine() for complex validation

165	## 11. Documentation

168	
169	- 👤 Every exported interface/type must have JSDoc
170	- 👤 File-level JSDoc for src/config/ modules
171	- 👤 Use @example where usage isn't obvious
172	- 👤 Use @see <link> to add links to documentation
173	- 👤 Focus on "why" and "how to use", not "what"
174	- 👤 No useless descriptions repeating function name
175	- 👤 Skip JSDoc only if no params AND obvious from name
176	- 👤 Use @deprecated <reason> to mark deprecated code
177	- 👤 All modules must have top level JSDoc with description and usage examples

Done. `rules/Bun.md` only, −18/+4.

**Two things I got wrong earlier, corrected:**

- There *is* a guard on these files — not a test, but `rulesSyncedHeadings` in [`scripts/validate-plugins.ts:103`](scripts/validate-plugins.ts). It requires `## Mandatory Context` and `## 15. Git Workflow` to be byte-identical across all four rule files. `bun run lint` caught my renumber.
- Consequently the numbering "holes" at §7 and §10 are **by design**, not a defect: the four files share one coordinate system and omit sections that don't apply to a stack. I reverted the sequential renumber I'd started.

**What actually shipped:**

| Removed | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `React.ComponentProps`, `React.memo`, React DevTools, "not in render" | React rules in the non-React Bun rule set |
| "No TailwindCSS/CSS-in-JS - use CSS Modules", "No useEffect for state sync" | same — and `Bun.md`'s only CSS mention was this line |
| "Schemas in `scripts/schemas/` by domain" | repo-specific leak, and wrong even here (`scripts/schemas.ts` is a file) |
| §2.2 "Directory Layout — `scripts/`" | repo-specific, near-zero information |
| §5's hardcoded script list | it advertised `bun run lint:fix`, which doesn't exist. Replaced with the line the other three already use: inspect `package.json` rather than assuming scripts |

One real structural bug fixed: `### 8.4 File Operations` was orphaned under `## 6. Common Standards` because the `## 8. Server-Side Standards` heading had been deleted. Added it back, with `6.3 Bun` → `8.1 Bun` to match the canonical slot the other three use.

The other three files needed nothing — they're structurally clean and identical in skeleton.

**Verification:** `bun run lint` green (12/12 tasks, 0 cached). Prettier clean. `bun run test` is 11/12 — the `release-action` failure is pre-existing and environmental: your git config sets `tag.gpgsign = true`, so `git tag v1.0.0` in `testHelpers.ts:91` becomes a signed annotated tag and dies with `fatal: no tag message?`. CI has no such config.

I deliberately left `§2.1 "ESLint for linting"` in place — that's the toolchain claim, and it belongs with the 🤖 work rather than here.

**Next, in the order I'd take them:**

1. **The 🤖 split** — the original topic: delete the ~14 verification-only rules, strip citations from the ~12 that shape generation, rewrite the legend. Applies to all four files, so the diff is 4× this one.
2. **`git tag --no-sign` in `testHelpers.ts`** — one-line portability fix so the release-action suite runs on any contributor's machine. Small, real, unrelated to rules.
3. **`Bun.md` has no §10 Testing at all**, and its §1 lacks "write failing tests first" / "run tests after changes" that the other three carry. That's adding content, not cleanup, so it deserves its own decision.

Which one?
